title: Intro finished-accuracy loss range contradicts Section 4.5 and Table 2
quote: generations lose 5.5–10.6 points against the untrained model on the same problem mix
explanation: Contributions says finished generations at the highest rate lose 5.5-10.6 points (A, B, no-filter; gold about 26). Section 4.5 says they lose 1.5-9.0 points, and Table 2 'Finished, matched' at 5e-4 gives -6.1, -1.5, -4.1, -3.2 (A/B) and -9.0, -3.6 (no-filter); the largest is -9.0 and nothing reaches 10.6 or 5.5 as a minimum. Gold is -26.0 and -23.7 in Table 2, so 'about 26' is also not the range. The headline contribution overstates the effect and conflicts with the results text.

title: pass@8 'within 4 points' contradicted by Table 2 (B, seed 0 is -5.3)
quote: pass@8 ends within 4 points of round 0 in every run
explanation: Section 4.2 claims every 10^-5 run ends within 4 points of round 0 on pass@k. Table 2 shows pass@k changes of -3.3, -1.3, -5.3 (B, seed 0), -2.0 and -2.7 (C); B at seed 0 exceeds 4 points. The abstract/intro detectable-effect framing relies on small pass@k changes.

title: Two different sample-accuracy bounds (2.2 vs 1.7)
quote: about 1.7 points is the largest upper limit among observed intervals
explanation: Section 3.4 refers to 'the 2.2-point bound' on sample accuracy as a post hoc claim, while Section 5.1 calls about 1.7 points the largest upper limit among observed sample-accuracy intervals. In Table 2 the largest sample-accuracy upper limit is +1.7 (A, seed 3 at 10^-4), and no 2.2 appears. The two figures are not reconciled.

title: 'Finished accuracy carries the whole change' vs Table 2 matched values
explanation: Section 4.5 says at 10^-4 and 2x10^-4 finished accuracy carries the whole decline. Table 2 shows sample-accuracy falls of 2.3-4.7 (10^-4) and 6.0, 6.0 (2x10^-4) but finished-matched changes of only -1.3, -0.6, -1.0 and -2.6, -3.2, i.e. a third to a half of the fall. The statement relies on an unconditional decomposition (Table S9) that is not shown in the main text, and it reads as contradicting the matched column.

title: Replicate gap of 3.8 not derivable and not matched by same-seed pairs
quote: ends 3.8 points of sample accuracy apart
explanation: The 3.8-point replicate gap is used as the gauge of training-seed variance but the pair is not identified. Same-seed A/B pairs at 5x10^-4 differ by 2.1 (seed 1: -10.8 vs -8.7) and 4.7 (seed 2: -6.0 vs -10.7) in Table 2; A at seeds 0/1 at 10^-5 differ by 0.2. No pair in Table 2 yields 3.8, and the gap is cited again as evidence for optimistic detection thresholds.

title: 'Largest pass@1 change' wording inconsistent with data
explanation: Section 5.1 calls -1.3 the 'largest pass@1 change' when it is the smallest in magnitude (the least negative) across Table 2, where changes reach -12.7 (C) and -12.0. Also, a nominally positive pass@k change (+2.0, 10^-4 seed 3) exists, so 'never happens detectably' applies only to interval exclusion, not to sign; the wording should say best (closest to gain) change.
